name: Industrial utility product
region: Factories, workshops, ships and rail yards of Europe and North America
summary: Fixtures made for work, not for show: enamel shades, cage lamps, cast iron, steel lockers, conduit and brass ship hardware. The form follows the duty, and the finish is hard and repairable.

philosophy.core_thesis: A tool-like object earns its form from the job it does and the strain it takes; any surface that does no work is left off.
design_principles: Make each part for one duty: a shade throws light down, a cage guards the bulb, a hook holds a load.
Choose cast iron, mild steel, aluminium and glass for strength; use 2 to 4 mm of steel for a shade or a locker.
Coat steel in vitreous enamel or powder paint that is hard, washable and 0.1 to 0.3 mm thick.
Show every bolt, rivet and weld; a worker must be able to repair each part with a spanner.
Use a simple dome, a cylinder or a box with a radius of 3 to 10 mm on the edges.
Use stock sizes: standard tube, pipe, sheet and bar, in a few colours such as white, black and grey.
Add a guard, a cage or a rib only where the object needs it, and keep the guard open.
anti_patterns: Applied ornament or a revival motif
Hidden fasteners and a smooth, sealed body
A thin, fragile section that fails in use

form.geometry: The dome, the cylinder, the box and the tube, joined by visible bolts, brackets and welds.
form.silhouette: A heavy, simple outline: a wide dome shade on a short stem, a box with a frame, or a tube bent at a right angle.
form.edges: Rolled or flanged edges with a radius of 3 to 10 mm; a cast edge has a parting line and a fillet of 2 to 5 mm.
form.proportion: A dome shade is 30 to 40 cm wide and about half as deep; a locker is 180 cm high and 30 to 40 cm wide.
form.ornament: None. The pattern is the repeat of rivets, ribs, vents and perforations that do a job; they cover 0 to 5% of the surface.
rules: Each object has 1 to 3 main bodies and a visible fastener for each part.
Steel sheet is 1.5 to 4 mm thick; cast iron is 5 to 10 mm thick.
No part is there only for looks; each rib, vent and guard has a duty.
Fasteners are bolts, rivets or welds, and they are in view.
Colour is white, black, grey, olive or a single signal colour, and the metal tone shows at each chip.

materials.rule: Metal makes about 70% of the visible surface; glass, timber and leather are plain and take the rest.

finish.gloss: 50–90 GU on enamel; 5–25 GU on powder paint and blackened metal
finish.patina: The style accepts wear: chips in the enamel, rust at an edge and a dark shine on brass are signs of use and are welcome.

hardware.section: Bolts M6–M12, tube 20–40 mm, bar 8–16 mm, cast bodies 6–10 mm thick
hardware.joints: Hex bolts, rivets and welds in view; a cast part has a flange with bolt holes, and a pipe has a union or a threaded elbow.
hardware.handles: A plain bar, a ring or a wheel of cast iron or steel, with a section of 12 to 25 mm; a lever handle on a locker.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A cross-head or wheel tap in brass; a heavy toggle or a rotary switch in a cast box; a cable in a steel conduit with elbows.

palette.strategy: The colour of the metal and of the coat on it: black, white, grey and olive, with one signal colour as a mark.

manufacture.scale: Factory series of thousands, made for works, ships, railways and the military, and later sold as stock and reissued.
manufacture.signs: A casting seam and a foundry mark, a dome with a rolled rim, bolt heads in a row and a chip that shows the dark metal.

positive: steel conduit and brass wheel tap
studio product photograph, hard side light

emotion.target_response: Plain trust in a tough object: the viewer sees how it works and expects it to last.

use_cases: lighting and hardware for a loft or a kitchen
a brief for reissued factory fixtures
a still life for a workshop-style shop
hardware schedules for a warehouse conversion
avoid_when: The room needs soft, ornate or luxury objects.
The brief asks for a thin, delicate or very bright finish.

modifiers.how: Keep the metal but round each edge, use chrome and aluminium, and add a long horizontal line.
Use pine, a peg and a painted finish in place of cast iron, and keep the plain form.
Add cast relief, a turned stem and a patterned glass shade.

ornament_level.note: A trace of ornament comes only from repeated parts, such as a row of rivets.

era_blend.note: A contemporary object in the same duty and material keeps the style.
